stemMd: A neutral metal sphere is charged negatively. What has happened to its electron population?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Every neutron has become an electron.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It must have lost all its atoms.

explanationMd: Electrons carry negative charge and can move between conductors. An excess relative to the unchanged positive nuclear charge makes the sphere negative. Ordinary charging does not change proton identities or require nuclear reactions.

distractorRationale.c: Electron loss would make the sphere positively charged.
distractorRationale.e: Proton charge does not reverse during ordinary charging.
distractorRationale.a: Charging a metal does not require nuclear conversion.
distractorRationale.b: The sphere remains a material object.
